en.title: Doctor Doom's Latverian Witches Revealed for Avengers: Doomsday
en.summary: A surprise post-credits scene in VisionQuest hints at Doctor Doom's formidable new allies. These masked figures, known as the Latverian Witches, are poised to play a pivotal role in the upcoming Avengers epic.
en.body:
The Marvel Cinematic Universe is gearing up for its next major event, **Avengers: Doomsday**, and a recent post-credits scene has sent ripples of excitement and speculation through the fandom. Following the events of **Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness**, where the **Scarlet Witch** met a grim fate on Mount Wundagore, a surprising reveal has brought her back into the fold. Through the potent magic of **Doctor Doom**, Wanda Maximoff is awakened, with Doom ominously declaring, "Scarlet Witch, awaken… your power will be mine." This moment not only confirms the long-speculated presence of **Doctor Doom** in **Avengers: Doomsday** but also introduces his mysterious Latverian Witches.

These masked coven members, seen in promotional materials, remain shrouded in secrecy, their faces hidden, each adorned with a unique mask. While the exact nature and origin of these witches are still under wraps, their connection to **Doctor Doom** and their potential role in the film suggest they are far more than mere pawns. They represent a new tier of magical threat, one that **Doctor Doom** is leveraging for his own nefarious purposes. This development also ties into broader MCU lore, potentially drawing from comic book storylines where powerful magic users often serve or are manipulated by formidable entities. The inclusion of characters like **Clea**, played by Charlize Theron, who recruits **Doctor Strange** to combat Incursions, further emphasizes the escalating magical stakes within the Multiverse Saga.

## The Looming Threat of Doom

The confirmation of **Robert Downey Jr.** as **Victor von Doom** in **Avengers: Doomsday** is a monumental moment for MCU fans. The enigmatic ruler of Latveria, a character long-awaited, is set to become a central antagonist. The introduction of the Latverian Witches alongside him amplifies this threat considerably. These figures are not just background players; they are integral to Doom's plan, suggesting a coordinated magical assault that will test the combined might of Earth's mightiest heroes. The film, directed by the **Russo Brothers**, is slated for a December 18, 2026 release and promises to be the culmination of the Multiverse Saga, bringing together heroes from disparate realities for an existential clash.

## Fan Frenzy and Speculation

Fans have been dissecting every frame of the VisionQuest post-credits scene, eager to understand the full implications of **Doctor Doom**'s return and the nature of his witches. The mystery surrounding their masks and their allegiance fuels rampant speculation online. Are they corrupted sorceresses, ancient beings bound to Doom's will, or perhaps even twisted versions of familiar magical characters? Their presence signifies a darker, more complex magical landscape than previously seen in the MCU, moving beyond individual powerhouses to organized arcane forces. This development is crucial for the narrative of **Avengers: Doomsday**, as it sets the stage for a conflict that transcends physical might, requiring heroes to confront formidable magical adversaries.

## What's Next

With **Avengers: Doomsday** on the horizon, the introduction of **Doctor Doom** and his Latverian Witches is just the beginning. Audiences can expect a deeper exploration of the MCU's magical elements and the intricate machinations of its most iconic villains. Further details regarding the witches' identities and their specific powers are expected to be revealed as the film's release date approaches.

In a surprise to even those who had advanced screeners and wrote all of their reviews in good faith that they were being shown the entire show and are not at all grouchy about finding out that their articles are now wrong, VisionQuest ended with an unexpected post-credits scene . The scene picks up shortly after the end of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness , where Scarlet Witch gets crushed on Mount Wundagore. In the new material, we look through Wanda’s point of view as the rubble lifts, courtesy of Doctor Doom’s magic. “Scarlet Witch, awaken… your power will be mine,” commands Doom, causing Wanda’s eyes to open suddenly. The post-credits scene all but confirms a theory that has been bandied about on the internet since promotional materials for Avengers: Doomsday revealed Doom’s Latverian Witches, a trio of women whose faces are hidden under masks, each of which wearing uniquely t remember Clea, since she has approximately one minute of screen time. But this will help: she’s the person Charlize Theron played in the post-credits scene, recruiting Strange to help deal with the problem of Incursions. Clea is one of the most important magical characters in the Marvel Universe. The daughter of Prince Orini of the Dark Dimension and niece to the Dread Dormammu, Clea became the love interest of Doctor Strange shortly after her first appearance in 1964’s Strange Tales #126, by Steve Ditko and Stan Lee . And, like most female characters in Marvel Comics, she sometimes gets corrupted when she gains too much power. However, Clea has more recently been given a steady place in the Marvel Universe, becoming the Sorcerer Supreme in Strange’s place and helping to bring balance to several dimensions. Of course, a big blockbuster like Doomsday would benefit from a surprise appearance by an A-lister like Theron. But Clea also makes sense on a narrative and adaptation level. In the 2015 Secret Wars storyline by Jonathan Hickman and Esad Ribić, Doctor Doom steals the powers of the godlike Beyonders to save the universe from destruction through Incursions. In the process, he remakes the world in his image, setting himself up as God Emperor and making the family of the despised Reed Richards—wife Sue Storm and children Franklin and Valeria—into his own family. Although a handful of survivors escape Doom’s recreation and eventually arrive to fight against it, only one person within Doom’s world remembers what used to be: Stephen Strange, who sought the Beyonders alongside Doom, but hesitated to take the power. For that reason, Strange plays the role of the Sheriff of Agamotto in this world, a guilt-riddled collaborator who enforces the lie that Doom has always been God Emperor because doing so will keep the peace.
